STANDARD, but at the TOP of the band and one notch riskier than the report states. Do not promote it to Full — it is still one production file — but do not sell it as "half a session" either.

The report's ~90-140 production lines + ~150 test lines is a fair count for what it DESCRIBES. It is an underestimate for what the lane actually requires, for four reasons I verified:
1. Each new arm must carry the SIM'S GATE, not just the target lookup: the defender arm needs `d.ehp !== null` (Helga only — see the REFUTED verdict), the shape arm needs `targetsStructures` + a strike-time range re-check (M5, M6), the castle arm is reachable only when there is no bond (creatureAttack.ts:470), and arm 1's predicate is not the sim's (M3). The report's table is a target-lookup table; the code needs a gate table.
2. M1 is an OPEN RULING that can change the bond arm's destination entirely (connector midpoint vs tower anchor). Building the wrong one and re-doing it is the difference between half a session and a whole one. Build it with the aim point behind a named local helper so a one-line change switches it, and ship whichever is chosen with a test pinning the choice.
3. `untargetableRetention.test.ts:314` is a confirmed re-pin against a twoSeat() world that contains castles — the new castle arm may well flip it, and a careless "relax the assertion" would delete a gate while leaving it green.
4. The arm-count tripwire the report asks for (tests_owed #3) is worth building and is more work than a line: the six sim arms live in one function but three of them are reached through helpers in a different file.

Net: plan one full branch, not half of one. The report's "FIX ONLY THIS" discipline is right and should be quoted verbatim into the brief — no stink-tower lob, no laser beam, no boss VFX, no cadence retune.

⛔ AND THE S182 LESSON APPLIES TO THIS REPORT ITSELF: its table contains one row (turret/stinkTower → fiery) that would ship a NEW defect of the exact class the file was already patched for. A branch handed this report unedited would fix what was asked and introduce a regression — the S182 pattern, on schedule. The brief must carry the corrected table, not this one.
